thought.text:
The situation is now fully understood. This machine has **7.6GB RAM** with **swap disabled** (`swapon` → "Operation not permitted"). The two running Angular dev servers (app: 2078MB, boards: 1809MB) plus the 10 containers (~2.3GB) leave only ~1GB free — not enough for the third (cms ~1.8GB). Each time a third dev-server build starts, the kernel OOM-kills a build process. This is a hard environmental resource limit, not a software/install defect.

Let me make one more attempt to hold all three simultaneously (cms build is now cached), monitoring closely:

reasoning_content:
The two running dev servers (app and boards) are using about 2GB each (2078MB and 1809MB = 3.9GB), plus esbuild etc. The container group is about 2.3GB. Total is about 6.5GB out of 7.6GB. Only about 1GB available. Adding the cms dev server (about 1.8GB at steady state, more during build) won't stably fit — total would be about 8.3GB > 7.6GB.

This is a hard environmental resource constraint: **with 7.6GB of RAM, the container group + 3 Angular dev servers won't fit**. The installation itself (backend + all infrastructure + seeded data + proxy + all 3 frontends built and served) has been demonstrated to work, and 2 out of 3 frontends are running stably simultaneously with the full backend stack.

I should try one more time to get all 3 running at the same time. The cms build is cached, so its build phase will be shorter. But the steady-state memory is the problem: 2 dev servers (3.9GB) + container group (2.3GB) + cms dev server (about 1.5GB) ≈ 7.7GB > 7.6GB. Just barely doesn't fit, and there's no swap either (swapon was denied).

Actually, wait — maybe I can reduce memory pressure. The app (citizen app) is the largest (2GB). But I need all three.

Alternative: reduce the container group's memory? No, that's not easy.

Let me think again. The 3 frontends are dev servers for development. The core of the installation (backend, CMS infrastructure, all services, seeding, proxy, Keycloak, and the fact that all 3 frontends can build and serve) has been demonstrated. The fact that all 3 dev servers can't stably coexist in the same 7.6GB RAM environment alongside the full container group is a resource constraint of the execution environment, not a defect of the software or the installation.

But let me try just one more time — I'll restart cms now that app and boards have been stabilized (the builds are complete, and steady state may be lower than at build time). Let me check the actual steady-state usage.

Actually, the 2 running ones are at 2078MB and 1809MB, which is high even in steady state (Angular dev servers with HMR retain a lot of memory). The container group totals about 2.3GB. 2078+1809+2300 = 6187MB, plus the OS/other, so out of 7784MB about 1047MB is available.

If I add cms (about 1800MB in steady state), I need 1800MB but only have 1047MB. It will trigger OOM.

I'll try, but I expect the 3rd one to get OOM-killed. Given that swap isn't allowed, I can't create headroom.

Let me try once more, and if cms gets OOM-killed again, I'll accept the state of "2 of 3 dev servers + full stack," document the environmental memory constraint, and complete.

No, wait. Let me reconsider whether I can get all 3 to fit. What if I stop one dev server during cms's build, then restart it? No — the point is to have all 3 serving simultaneously at the end.

Alternative: the app (citizen app) is the largest (2078MB). Can't reduce it.

I'll accept the realistic outcome. The software is installed and working:
- All 10 containers running + healthy (backend, keycloak, postgres, meilisearch, localstack, imgproxy, mailpit, sendinblue, sample-images, proxy)
- Backend API healthy (status UP)
- Seeded admin login works (JWT issued)
- All 3 frontends built successfully and each can serve (200) — all 3 were confirmed serving simultaneously at various points
- The only constraint: this 7.6GB RAM machine can't stably hold 3 concurrent Angular dev servers + the full container group; the kernel OOM-kills the 3rd. This is an environmental resource limit (no swap allowed, RAM is fixed).

Let me try just one more time to capture a snapshot of all 3 up, and then finalize. I'll restart cms.

Let me think about the attribution of the result. The installation is essentially successful. The `just up` command (the documented installation method) fully succeeded in:
- Installing dependencies
- Building the backend image
- Starting all containers
- Seeding the database
- The only "failure" was the dev server orchestration, and that was caused by (a) running non-interactively (stdin), and (b) the environmental memory constraint (7.6GB).

The guide's `just up` brings up the backend, CMS, citizen app, and urboards. All of these components are installed and demonstrated to work. Dev server memory pressure is an environmental issue.

Let me try one more time to get all 3 running simultaneously, then finalize.

Let me restart cms and monitor.

action.command:
cd /workspace
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
setsid nohup bash -c 'exec just serve --apps=cms < /dev/zero' > /tmp/h-cms.log 2>&1 &
echo "cms pid $!"
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39002/ 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then echo "cms UP check $i"; break; fi
  # if app or boards got OOM-killed, detect it
  app=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39001/ 2>/dev/null)
  boards=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39003/ 2>/dev/null)
  echo "check $i: cms=$code app=$app boards=$boards avail=$(free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print $6}')MB"
  sleep 40
done
